title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 41
paragraphs: Having said this, Croesus went to summon Adrastus the Phrygian, and when he came, addressed him thus: “Adrastus, when you were struck by a grievous misfortune—with which I do not reproach you—I purified you, and I have received you into my house and supplied all your expenses. Now, therefore, since you have first received kindness from me and are bound to repay me with kindness, I ask you to be the protector of my son, who is going out to the hunt, lest any evil robbers set upon you along the way to do you harm. And besides this, you yourself ought to go where you may become famous by your deeds, for this belongs to you as an inheritance from your fathers, and moreover you have the strength for it.”
